comments.text: Actor type three. Initialize walking direction toward the player, animation dividers, health one and fall state. Test player overlap and projectile-character damage, animate four facing-dependent walk shapes, turn at blocking terrain and fall according to the vertical tables. The descending-player contact path changes the actor to its flattened state and can bounce the player; its second coordinate comparison uses player X. Wheel/immunity contact or the screen flash releases it through an explosion and awards 100 points.

Operand byte 1 of the BPL instruction at $6C02, within this level's existing actor or display routine. It is not an independent instruction entry. The shared call to $6C03 selects music only in overlays that contain the music driver; this level has an actor branch operand here.

Continuation of the type-three initialization at $6C00: store its animation divider, derive phase and health values by shifts, clear its behavior state and choose facing. A music call to this address belongs to flight overlays, whose bytes are different.
Two four-frame walking sprite bases, selected by facing; the phase is added by the actor updater.
Two half-pixel horizontal steps, minus one and plus one, selected by facing.
Thirteen signed vertical steps indexed zero through twelve by the descending fall counter. The walker installs twelve when entering its ordinary falling state and saturates the counter at zero.
Twenty-seven signed vertical steps, indexed zero through twenty-six, for the temporary and flattened behavior states. This begins immediately after the separate thirteen-entry ordinary falling table.

Actor type four, using one head and six allocated body slots. Refuse a second independently initialized head, then emerge by lifting the linked slots and allocating the body. In its active state use six phase-shifted vertical and horizontal motion streams, reverse facing toward the player, and launch additional type-four projectile slots. The head's vulnerable state has health sixteen; destruction awards 750 points and schedules the body slots to explode with different delays. Player contact, projectile damage and the screen flash use separate branches.
Nine colours cycled by the segmented creature's projectile state through its descending modulo-nine cursor.
Two signed horizontal increments selected by facing for body placement and projectile motion.
Two X offsets applied when the head changes facing, paired with its direction-dependent head sprites.
Lookup base used with body indices one through six to read the six staggered explosion delays at $71EA-$71EF. The base byte itself belongs to the preceding turn-offset table.
Six staggered countdown values copied into the linked body-slot explosion delays when the head dies. The copying loop addresses them through base $71E9 with indices one through six.
Two XOR masks selected by projectile facing to alternate its sprite shape.
Six split addresses to forty-eight-byte signed vertical-motion streams, one for each linked component phase.
High-byte half of the six vertical-motion pointers beginning at $71F2.
Six split addresses to twenty-four-byte horizontal-motion streams. The active facing determines whether a selected step is added or subtracted.
High-byte half of the six horizontal-motion pointers at $71FE.

Actor type five. Its subtype chooses initial shape and delay; face toward the player and apply a timed curved vertical trajectory while moving horizontally. One subtype follows an alternate terrain-aware path and periodically creates type-sixteen projectiles. Contact can hurt the player; character shots subtract from health two, and destruction awards 100 points. Actors leaving the permitted area are released.
Three initial sprite numbers selected by the actor's subtype.
Three subtype-dependent start delays, counted down before the curved flight begins.
Two signed horizontal increments selected by facing.
Five descending-trajectory thresholds used to select the five-frame pose within each facing/subtype sequence.
Five shapes for the first subtype in one facing direction; the paired reverse-facing sequence begins at $7590.
Five shapes for the first subtype's opposite facing direction.
Five shapes for the alternate subtype, paired with $759A for the other facing.
Five opposite-facing shapes for the alternate subtype's flight animation.
Forty-eight signed vertical steps selected by the descending flight counter. One subtype adds the step to Y and the other subtracts it.

Actor type six. Start above the playfield with health four and three animated shapes, descend until terrain is reached, then release the actor and create a type-five flying enemy when a slot is available. Destruction by contact protection, projectile damage or screen flash awards 500 points and emits up to six type-sixteen projectiles with the velocity pairs at $76D2/$76D8.
Six signed horizontal velocities for the type-sixteen projectile burst emitted on this actor's destruction.
Six vertical velocities paired with the horizontal burst values at $76D2.

Actor type seven. Initialize fixed sprite $BF, health fifteen and a firing countdown. Apply contact/projectile/screen-flash checks, then periodically allocate type-eight flying enemies at its position. Destruction awards 1000 points and converts the actor to an explosion; out-of-bounds actors are released.

Actor type eight. Initialize subtype-dependent vertical motion and CIA-timer-selected horizontal motion. Alternate two shapes, wait through the start delay, then change the movement components on independently randomized dividers. Terrain blocks reverse the corresponding component; projectile hits or protected contact convert it to an explosion and award 100 points.
Two initial signed vertical velocities, selected by the subtype's low seven bits.

Actor type nine. Subtype zero is a hidden controller that creates random nonzero-subtype particles at the right edge and can push an eligible player left while checking the terrain. Particle subtypes select shape, colour, X/Y increments and vertical divider from six parallel tables. Colour-five particles also animate their sprite on a subtype/slot-dependent divider. Release particles leaving the visible bounds.
Sixteen subtype-selected initial sprite numbers. Controller subtype zero uses the blank marker while allocating visible particles.
Sixteen subtype-selected sprite colours; colour five selects the particle animation branch.
Sixteen signed animation-divider selectors. The updater reads this table by actor slot, using the sign to choose the three-frame animation direction.
Sixteen signed horizontal movement steps selected by particle subtype.
Sixteen vertical increments selected by subtype and applied when its divider expires.
Sixteen initial/reload values for the particle vertical-motion divider.

Actor type ten. The initial state supplies a solid platform and changes to its reward state when struck by a projectile. Repeated qualified hits count down its reward counter, create bouncing collectible slots with randomized subtypes, and finally award 5000 points before explosion. Separate overlap paths let the player stand on it or bump it from below, maintaining the shared platform-contact flags. Spawned reward actors move with a signed trajectory until they become ordinary type-two pickups.
Nine signed vertical offsets for the platform's bump response, selected by its descending response counter.
Thirty signed vertical offsets for newly launched rewards before they settle into the ordinary collectible behavior.

Actor type twelve. Alternate its shape on a two-call divider, enable multicolour, follow player X and form Y from player posture and wheel offsets. During the ascending part of a jump increment player Y. The picture's identity remains to be named from the graphics.
Mutable sprite number and two-call divider for the player-attached type-twelve effect.
Mutable two-call animation divider paired with the type-twelve splash sprite number at $7C3F.
Two Y offsets selected by player posture before the wheel-mode correction is added.
Two standing/wheel Y corrections for the type-twelve attached sprite.

Actor type eleven. Animate its sprite on a two-call divider, enable multicolour, select its colour from the level background condition, and follow the player's X/Y with one of three vertical offsets. Its visual identity remains open.
Mutable sprite number, divider and vertical-offset selector for the player-attached type-eleven effect.
Mutable two-call animation divider paired with the type-eleven splash sprite number at $7C78.
Index zero through two selecting the type-eleven splash's vertical offset from $7C7B. The level callback records which of three player-adjacent cells met its water condition.
Three pixel-Y offsets selected by the effect's state byte at $7C7A.

Test the terrain beside the player's upper/side cells for glyphs $C4-$C7 and allocate or remove a type-twelve attached effect accordingly. Rotate a strip of character bytes at $C61D-$C63F, copy its leading pair to glyph $18 and randomize six following glyph rows through the mask at $AFF3.
Operand byte 1 of the LDX instruction at $7CD5, within this level's existing actor or display routine. It is not an independent instruction entry.
Copy ten pickup shape defaults from $7D2B to $089B and sixteen actor-scroll corrections from $7D35 to $0876.
Ten collectible sprite pointers copied to the shared resident reward-shape table at $089B.
Sixteen actor-coordinate corrections, eight X and eight Y values, restored to the shared tables beginning at $0876.

Actor type fifteen. Wait for centred horizontal scrolling and a grounded player, then clear the other actors and install the special camera/display hooks. Represent the boss with three sprite columns reused across five vertical bands, plus two projectile sprites. Select successive actions from $85A5, update contact and character-shot collisions, and dispatch its destruction sequence when its two-byte health underflows. Its initial health is $019B; damage is accepted on selected rows and sides. Destruction restores the regular actor multiplexer and camera, creates eleven explosion actors and awards 10000 points.

During an impact/shake countdown choose the vertical fine-scroll phase. When no action is active, select the next action ID from the nineteen-byte sequence at $85A5, patch the JMP through the five split pointers at $859B/$85A0, and advance the sequence cursor, wrapping to entry one. Clear the action-local phase before dispatch.
Operand byte 1 of the JMP instruction at $7E95, within this level's existing actor or display routine. It is not an independent instruction entry.
Operand byte 2 of the JMP instruction at $7E95, within this level's existing actor or display routine. It is not an independent instruction entry.

On the action's first call install its initial pose, then lower all five sprite rows by five pixels until the terrain probe reports support. Snap the first row to its aligned resting Y, request the paired impact sounds and arm the display shake before releasing this action.

Install the facing-dependent pose and run a forty-eight-step vertical jump curve while shifting all three body columns horizontally. Toggle their X high bits on crossings. On landing request impact/shake, reverse facing, restore the corresponding full pose and release the action.

Use a three-phase timed pose sequence: wait twelve calls, install the partial pose through $82F2 for seventy calls, restore the regular pose for ten calls, then release the action. The projectile allocator suppresses firing during this action ID.
Repeat the thirty-two-step vertical hop curve three times. Each landing requests paired impact sounds and a shake; after the third, restore the facing-dependent pose and release the action.
Install the regular facing-dependent pose, wait through a fifty-call countdown and clear the active-action flag.

Maintain two projectile records on hardware sprites six and seven. On its launch divider, allocate an idle record when the active boss action permits firing, derive its position from boss facing and body coordinates, and request its effect sound. Active projectiles move sixteen pixel-X units per call, track the ninth X bit separately, and are removed after crossing the side limit. Finish by writing both hardware-sprite positions.
Write the two projectile X high bits, X low bytes and Y values into hardware sprites six and seven, using the register-offset and mask pairs at $8610-$8615.

Probe each active projectile against the player, then the boss body when its top row is within range. Convert nine-bit sprite X to the player's half-pixel coordinates and use the shared rectangle test. Wheel mode or invulnerability suppresses the damage call.
Compare player coordinates with the supplied half-pixel X and pixel-Y rectangle extents in $DD-$E0. On overlap, call the player-damage hook unless wheel/invulnerability is active.

Scan thirteen terrain rows around the boss silhouette using facing-dependent left/right offsets. Consume projectile characters by writing $FF to the hit cell. Rows two through four on the vulnerable side subtract the character's damage value from the two-byte health at $BC98/$BC99; other contacts consume the shot without reducing health. A damaging hit flashes the fifteen body colours; health underflow starts the death countdown.

Alternate the boss colour matrix and request the death sound while the countdown runs. Restore the shared camera and raster hooks, replace the actor slots with eleven offset explosions, request the palette flash and temporary player blocking state, then award 10000 points through the score hook.

Facing selects one of two fifteen-entry groups. Copy its colours, sprite numbers and bitmap-address low/high bytes from $8616/$8634/$8652/$8670 into the three-column by five-row live boss matrices at $AD4A/$ADED/$AE90/$AF33.

Copy three selected rows in each of three columns from the nine six-entry source arrays at $868E-$86C3 into the live sprite-number and bitmap-address matrices. Facing selects one three-entry half through $85BA.
Copy two selected rows per column from the nine four-entry arrays at $86C4-$86E7 into the boss matrices. Facing selects one two-entry half through $85BC.

Convert the first body row's Y and the first column's nine-bit X to a playfield row pointer and character column. Probe a cell thirteen character rows below it, returning carry set when its terrain property is nonzero; retain the pointer and column for the silhouette damage scan.
Convert A plus the separately supplied nonzero ninth-bit selector in Y into the player's eight-bit half-pixel X through a carry-assisted ROR.

Draw projectile positions, find the visible band among the five boss rows, and initialize the next three sprite Y registers and row cursors. When the band crosses a sensitive fine-scroll alignment, temporarily exchange bitmap rows through $84EF.

Select the first visible band's three sprite pointers in both screen directories, write the three body-column X coordinates and high bits, and install its three colours. Handle a top-clipped band by waiting for the following visible row before assigning its Y values.

Multiplex hardware sprites three through five across the remaining boss rows. Replace their shape pointers and colours, restore a previously exchanged bitmap row when needed, and schedule the next raster stop according to the vertical fine-scroll alignment. After the final visible row reinstall the status-panel raster handler.
